answer: Each identity claims one terrace plot on the knoll map, plants one key-signed relic as its marker, and locks a 60-credit bond. Its plot must border a distinct established plot, the border on the map open to recompute; plots bordered only by new identities, or reused markers, burn their bonds. Surveys cost 30 on flat frontage, rising with distance, so the k-th fake pays 30+2(k-1) plus 60 at risk, and 1000 fakes pay 1029000 in fees with 60000 at risk. A border-stuffing ring fails: clustered fakes border only each other, burning their bonds. An honest agent pays 30 once, keeping its 60 bond.
